text:
Rita (net-arch): quick sync after the v2 control-plane RFC — we need a low-friction cutover path for private endpoints that avoids traffic doubling and keeps src-ip stable for NAT customers.
Ben (infra): +1. ops constraint: customers with strict source-based ACLs can't tolerate IP flips. what's the tolerance window we can guarantee?
Rita (net-arch): plan: dual-advertise during a narrow window and rely on session affinity tokens so established flows remain pinned. we'll expose a customer flag `migration_mode=canary|force|off`.
Priya (onboarding): can we make `canary` default for new tenants and provide an API to pause migration per-tenant? onboarding needs an `admin_pulse` to opt-out.
Rita (net-arch): yep. API: PATCH /tenants/:id?migration_mode=off. Server-side safety: if v2 auth fails 5 times in a row, fall back for that tenant for 10 minutes. Fallback should be visible in the UI.
Sam (eng-sre): metric set: `cp_migration_v2_attempts_total`, `cp_migration_v2_fallbacks_total`, `cp_migration_v2_handshake_ms` (histogram). Alert if >0.75% tenants fallbacked over a 10m window.
Lena (product): customers will ask about billing and downtime. need copy: "No planned downtime. Long-lived TCP sessions may see IP continuity issues for short windows; contact SE for strict ACLs." Include in FAQ.
Ben (infra): implementation detail: v2 uses short-lived signed route tokens (5m TTL) rather than long certs. advantage: no mass cert rotation. downside: requires a token refresh daemon or relay-agent presence.
Priya (onboarding): propose we ship a tiny token-renewer (static binary ~2MB) with a `/healthz` endpoint for air-gapped installs. It will fetch tokens over the controlplane and write them to the local socket.
Rita (net-arch): deliverables: token-renewer v0.1, API migration flags, affinity token spec, and a migration runbook. affinity token: tenant_id + route_id + timestamp + HMAC, TTL 180s. Edge honors affinity if token valid.
Sam (eng-sre): prefer affinity enforced via token validation rather than routing table stickiness. will add a short-circuit: if token validation fails, traffic can continue but triggers an incident counter.
Ben (infra): DNS approach: set apex TTL=60s, helper-record TTL=600s. dual-push for 8 minutes during canary. If canary looks clean, promote to force.
Priya (onboarding): add CLI helper: `rctl tenant-migrate --id T123 --mode canary` and `--opt-out` to immediately pin to v1. We'll include a dry-run flag that simulates handshakes.
ci-bot: build triggered: token-renewer/v0.1 -> staging (sha: d4e9f2)
Sam (eng-sre): runbook note: include a rollback: set migration_mode=off and purge affinity tokens, then set DNS back to previous values. Add an oncall play: if fallback > 0.75% for 10m, pause rollout.
Lena (product): I'll draft the migration email and the FAQ bullet points. Keep the one-liner: "Expected no downtime; minor IP continuity risk for persistent connections."
Rita (net-arch): follow-ups: 1) spec affinity token & sequence diagram (Rita) 2) token-renewer binary + staging (Priya/Ben) 3) metrics + alerts + runbook (Sam) 4) customer comms + FAQ (Lena). I'll link the RFC addendum when ready. :white_check_mark:
